Sam: Heads up — saw a regression in /generate token-level latency after last runtime change. Token P95 jumped ~2.3x during canary. Trace correlation suggests kernel fallback events. Anyone digging in? :eyes:
Maya: saw that too. Profiling shows a lot of small kernels being picked for attention ops when seq_len > 1024. KV cache hit dropped which increased effective seq_len for some requests. I'll paste a perf snippet.
Maya: ```perf snippet
kernel_select: aten::scaled_dot_product_attention -> fallback: cuBLAS_compatible_small_kv (cost=1.8ms)
kernel_switches: 24 per request
kv_cache.hit_ratio: 0.66 for /generate
```
Cheng: KV hit ratio dropped from 0.92 to 0.66 for that route between 03:14-03:20 UTC. Metric name is `runtime.kv_cache.hit_ratio{route="/generate"}`. Dashboard shows strong correlation with token_latency.p50/p95.
Eva: ops-bot alert: alert runtime-high-token-latency /generate p95 > 120ms at 2024-05-05T03:15Z
Priya: Quick hypothesis: batching heuristic changed to prefer micro-batches (to reduce mem pressure) which reduces coalescing across concurrent short requests -> more kernel switches and less cache reuse. We should validate by replaying with old batching params.
Sam: Good call. Proposed plan: 1) add request_id -> trace link in per-token metrics 2) enrich traces with kernel selection events (kernel.name, selected_by) 3) add dashboard drilldown per-request to link to trace viewer.
Maya: I added a small patch to exporter to include `x-req-id` as a tag on token latency metrics in PR #412. Logs will include `trace_id=<trace>` and `kernel=fallback_small_kv`. Example log: `2024-05-05T03:15:12Z [req=abcd1234] kernel_select=fallback_small_kv seq_len=1150 kv_hit=false token_ms=142`
Cheng: Repro steps (quick): run loadtest with long seq dist and compare batching modes.
Cheng: ```./tools/loadtest --route /generate --qps 50 --seq-dist long --batching adaptive-old```
Cheng: ```./tools/loadtest --route /generate --qps 50 --seq-dist long --batching adaptive-new```
Eva: I've added a Grafana panel: per-route token_latency by req tag + link to Jaeger via ${trace_id} in the table. Works if trace_id is present on metrics as an exemplar.
Priya: Suggestion: use Prometheus exemplars to attach trace_id to a sample so the panel can link directly to trace viewer.
Sam: Also add a CI perf test that runs a fixed prompt set and fails if token-level P95 regresses >15% vs baseline.
Maya: I'll open the canary rollout (20% capacity) and add the perf CI job. Also adding a lightweight profiler that emits `kernel_event` spans to traces.
Cheng: I'll coordinate changes to KV instrumentation and update the /generate route dashboards (per-route KPIs: token_ms.p50/p95, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_switch_count).
Priya: I'll prototype a kernel-selector fallback policy: prefer "stable" kernels for seq>1024 on the pinned GPU family — trades some throughput for consistent latency. Plan to canary at 20% and measure p95.
Sam: Owners: Maya (metrics + exporter), Cheng (KV + dashboards), Priya (kernel selector + canary), Eva (alerts + grafana). I'll file a short RFC with timeline today. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deployment canary started for runtime-v2 on capacity 20% (canary id: c-20240505-01)
Maya: Noted — I'll follow the canary and post hourly p50/p95 dumps.
Cheng: Also will check quantized-kernel interactions; quantization sometimes changes kernel choice heuristics.
Maya: good catch.
Sam: TL;DR: regression likely caused by batching + KV miss -> kernel fallback; action items: add trace linkage to metrics, emit kernel selection spans, run canary with kernel-selector tweak, add perf CI.
Priya: I'll schedule the canary window and add guardrails (auto rollback if p95 > 125ms)
Sam: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread.
